draft.title: The derivative from first principles
card: The gradient of a secant through (x, f(x)) and (x + h, f(x + h)) is (f(x + h) − f(x))/h. Here h is the gap in x between the two points.
As h gets closer to 0, the second point slides towards the first. The secant turns into the tangent at that point.
The derivative is that limit: f'(x) = lim (f(x + h) − f(x))/h as h approaches 0. It gives the gradient of the tangent at x.
Example: f(x) = x². Then (f(x + h) − f(x))/h = (2xh + h²)/h = 2x + h. As h approaches 0, this approaches 2x, so f'(x) = 2x.
draft.remember: Find the secant gradient, simplify it, then let h approach 0.

a.q: What does f'(x) = lim (f(x + h) − f(x))/h as h approaches 0 give?
opts: The gradient of the tangent at x
The gradient of the secant between two fixed points
The average rate of change over an interval
The value of the function at x
a.why: As h approaches 0, the secant becomes the tangent, so the limit is the tangent's gradient. A secant gradient needs two separate points, so it is not the limit.
a.clue: What does the secant turn into as h shrinks?

b.q: Using first principles, what is f'(x) for f(x) = x² + 3x?
b.why: The secant gradient is ((x + h)² + 3(x + h) − x² − 3x)/h = (2xh + h² + 3h)/h = 2x + h + 3. As h approaches 0, this approaches 2x + 3. The option 2x + 3h keeps h, which has gone to 0 in the limit.
b.clue: Expand, cancel the h in the denominator, then let h approach 0.

a.best: The gradient of the tangent at x
